manufacturer: BKC Semiconductors, NTE, Taitron (the sheets' limits); typical curve: MTM Scientific

source.licence: Our own fit to a published typical curve and the makers' limits (D-253): the values are Solum Builder's

rating_sources.if_avg: BKC Semiconductors 1N34A data sheet (Gold Bonded Germanium Diodes, DO-7): Absolute Maximum Ratings at 25 °C: Average Rectified Forward Current 50 mA
rating_sources.vr_max: BKC Semiconductors 1N34A data sheet (Gold Bonded Germanium Diodes, DO-7): Absolute Maximum Ratings at 25 °C: Peak Inverse Voltage 65 V

fit.sheet: MTM Scientific, 1N34A Diode Performance (a typical forward curve, 0 to 3 mA, linear axes)
fit.figure: 1N34A Diode Performance, traced by pixel off the published image (dioper.jpg)
fit.method: IS, N and RS by least squares on V = N·Vt·ln(I/IS) + RS·I (scripts/fit_models.py fit_diode, Vt at 27 °C) over every other point of the curve from 0.15 V (one per 25 mV); IS under BKC's 30 µA leakage at 10 V (it fits at 5 µA, under the cap). CJO 0.8 pF, Taitron's typical at 0 V (NTE: 1 pF max at −1 V); EG 0.67 eV (germanium); BV 65 V at 1 mA, BKC's breakdown minimum
fit.note: None of the makers' sheets found (BKC, NTE, Taitron) draws a typical curve: they give only limits, which this fit passes. The curve is MTM Scientific's (a crystal-radio supplier), whose page says only that it is typical (0.35 V at 1 mA); builders' readings of real 1N34As run 0.22 to 0.34 V, so units spread either side. Above 3 mA the fit follows its 75 Ω series resistance, past the curve: a point-contact part's soft, nearly linear rise
